**Finding: compliant** (rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)

Section 4 runs in our favour and satisfies the preferred position on the material terms:

- **§ 4(a)** vests all Works (SOW deliverables/work product) in Clear Capital, with **§ 4(a)–(b)** requiring Contractor to execute further documents to perfect those rights.
- **§ 4(b)** limits Contractor to its own pre-existing tools, methodologies and know-how — an acceptable vendor carve-out, not ownership of our deliverables.
- **§ 4(c)** gives us the licence-back the playbook requires: royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable rights to use, copy, modify, create derivative versions of and display any Contractor's Information embedded in the Works for our business operations.
- No assignment of our IP or data to Contractor and no joint ownership; **§ 5(b)** carves our programs, data and materials out of Contractor's conveyance, and **§ 8** treats our data as Confidential Information usable only to perform the Services.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined (minor sub-elements): ownership is framed as vesting for periods invoiced and paid, § 4(d) ties unrestricted modification to payment in full or termination, the § 4(c) licence is not expressly "irrevocable"/"worldwide", and there is no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence. Worth tidying if the document opens for other reasons, but the clause clears the fallback, so no redline was proposed.
